newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures end lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures settled mostly lower Friday, under pressure from local selling and spillover weakness from feeder cattle futures, CME traders said.
"When the feeders fell apart, so did we," a trader said.

Feeder cattle futures settled sharply lower on weakness in cash feeder cattle markets and a sharp drop in the CME feeder cattle index, traders said. The index fell $0.36 to $62.92 per cwt on Thursday.
Friday's session was described as quiet by most traders.
Commercial buying of December live cattle late in the session lifted that contract off the day's lows, floor sources said.

Bullish traders remained optimistic about the possibility of higher or at least steady cash cattle prices next week because many cattle left over from this week's sales are below optimal slaughter weights.
"The cattle feeder is in pretty good shape," one bullish trader said. "What he has left is pretty green and not much to worry about."
One cash-connected trader forecast that fed cattle would trade at $69.00, which is $1.00 less than the bulk of this week's trade at $70.00.
USDA reported slight gains in choice and select grade beef at midday Friday, and those gains also provided futures with some support, floor traders said.
"The beef market was a little higher at midday and that helped us some," a floor source said.
August, October and December 1997 cattle delivery months notched fresh contract lows.

Live cattle futures closed down 0.300 to 0.600 cent a lb, with December cattle settling unchanged and February down 0.300 at 62.775 cents. Feeder cattle futures settled down 0.500 to 0.900 cent, with November down 0.900 at 62.67 cents.
